---
title: "Installation and troubleshooting"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

dMod2 compiles C++ code for every model during the R session. It needs a C++17 compiler, Python
with SymPy for code generation, and further Python packages for some features.

## Package installation

```{r}
remotes::install_github("dModverse/dMod2")
```

[cppDE](https://dmodverse.github.io/cppDE/) and [cOde](https://github.com/dkaschek/cOde) are
listed under `Remotes:` and installed with it. Models compile against the installed cppDE headers,
so cppDE is installed first; after a cppDE reinstall, the next `compile()` recompiles the model
sources.

## C++ compiler

| system | what to install |
|---|---|
| Linux | compilers R was built with, e.g. `sudo apt install r-base-dev` |
| macOS | Xcode command line tools, `xcode-select --install` |
| Windows | [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) matching the R version |

`compile()` calls `R CMD SHLIB` with the compiler and flags of R, `~/.R/Makevars` included.
`pkgbuild::check_build_tools(debug = TRUE)` tests whether R finds a compiler.

## Python environment

cppDE and dMod2 declare their Python packages with `reticulate::py_require()`;
[reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/) provides a Python with them on first use.

| package | needed for |
|---|---|
| `sympy` | code generation, symbolic derivatives, `steadyStates()` |
| `numpy`, `scipy` | symbolic layer of dMod2 |
| `python-libsbml` | `importSbml()`, `exportSbml()`, `importPEtab()`, `exportPEtab()` |
| `symident` | `symmetryDetection()`, `symmetryReduction()` |

These functions also need R packages that dMod2 only suggests, so `install_github()` leaves them
out: `rjson` for SBML, `yaml` for PEtab and `jsonlite` for the symmetries.

With `RETICULATE_PYTHON` set, reticulate uses that Python and provisions nothing; dMod2 installs a
missing symident or python-libsbml into it with `reticulate::py_install()`, or beforehand:

```sh
python -m pip install sympy numpy scipy python-libsbml symident
```

`reticulate::py_config()` shows the Python of the session. The SBML and PEtab interfaces run
libsbml in a separate Python process, whose interpreter `DMOD_LIBSBML_PYTHON` sets.

## symident and msolve

On first use of `symmetryDetection()` or `symmetryReduction()`, dMod2 installs
[symident](https://github.com/dModverse/symident) from PyPI into the session Python. On failure
the error names the interpreter; `pip install -U symident` with that interpreter installs it.

Coupled steady states in a steady-state start need [msolve](https://msolve.lip6.fr/).
Interactively, `symmetryDetection()` offers to build it into the symident cache, on Windows with
Rtools. `SYMIDENT_MSOLVE` points to an msolve built elsewhere:

```{r}
Sys.setenv(SYMIDENT_MSOLVE = "/opt/msolve/bin/msolve")
```

Every environment variable `SYMIDENT_<NAME>` reaches symident as the switch `<name>`, see Details
of `?symmetryDetection`.

## Optional solver libraries

The default backend needs no further libraries. `odemodel(backend = "Sundials")` needs SUNDIALS,
a sparse Jacobian SuiteSparse/KLU; cppDE finds both at install time. Without administrator rights,

```{r}
cppDE::installLibs("sundials")      # or "suitesparse"
```

builds them into a user cache; afterwards cppDE is reinstalled with the printed command.

## Output directory

The constructors (`odemodel()`, `Y()`, `P()`, ...) write C++ sources into
`getOption("dMod2.outdir")`, by default the working directory; `compile()` puts object files and
shared object next to them and skips unchanged sources. `odemodel(backend = "deSolve")` compiles
in the working directory only. For scratch work:

```{r}
options(dMod2.outdir = tempdir())
```

## Common errors

**`Compilation failed: ...` with "command not found" or `make` missing.** No compiler: Rtools
missing or mismatched (Windows), command line tools missing (macOS).
`pkgbuild::check_build_tools(debug = TRUE)` shows what R tries.

**`Compilation failed: ...` with C++ errors in generated code.** The compiler lacks C++17; update
it, on Windows with Rtools.

**Python or SymPy errors when building the model.** No Python, or one without SymPy. Check
`reticulate::py_config()`; with `RETICULATE_PYTHON` set, install SymPy there.

**`Could not provision a Python with python-libsbml`.** Install `python-libsbml` into the session
Python, or set `DMOD_LIBSBML_PYTHON` to an interpreter that has it.

**`... source files would need as many shared objects, but R can load at most ...`.** Pass
`output = "<name>"` to `compile()` to link all sources into one shared object.

**`A shared library named '...' is already loaded`.** A model name was used twice; dMod2 appends
`_2`, `_3`, ... A new name avoids the warning.

**`A sparse Jacobian was requested, but cppDE was installed without the KLU linear solver`.** Run
`cppDE::installLibs("suitesparse")` and reinstall cppDE.

**`NULL value passed as symbol address`.** A model shared object was unloaded by `dyn.unload()`.
Restart R; `loadDLL()` loads without unloading.

**`mstrust()` or `profile()` with `cores > 1` hangs.** A threaded BLAS without thread control
deadlocks in forked workers; dMod2 warns on attach. Start R with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, see
`cppDE::forkGuard()`.
